text:
**Short answer: about 300-400 W of solar panels refills a 1,000 Wh power station in one sunny day. 200 W takes about a day and a half.**

**The math**

Daily energy = panel watts × peak sun hours × about 0.7-0.75. The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle and charging losses ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).

| Panel size | Typical daily output (4.5 sun hours, 70%) | Time to fill 1,000 Wh from empty |
|---|---|---|
| 100 W | ~315 Wh | ~3 days |
| 200 W | ~630 Wh | ~1.5 days |
| 400 W | ~1,260 Wh | under a day |

(Table from [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/). [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station) gives the same 630 Wh figure for 200 W.)

**Panel watts needed to refill in one day, by season**
- **Average day (4-4.5 sun hours):** about 320-340 W ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).
- **Good summer (5 sun hours):** about 270-300 W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Northern winter (about 2 sun hours):** roughly 700 W or more, which is impractical for portable panels.

If you only need it full in 1.5-2 days, the rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5, so about 200 W.

**Check before you buy**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps how many watts it accepts. Many 1,000 Wh units accept 400-800 W, but entry-level ones may cap at 200 W, so panels above the cap add nothing.
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay within your station's input range. Exceeding it can damage the charge controller.
- **Connectors:** Panels typically use MC4, while stations use XT60, DC barrel or proprietary ports, so you may need an adapter.
- **Running loads:** If you use the station while it charges, net charging is slower.
